arxiv-2102-11115.title: Probing Multimodal Embeddings for Linguistic Properties: the Visual-Semantic Case
arxiv-2102-11115.creator: Adam Dahlgren Lindström, Suna Bensch, Johanna Björklund, Frank Drewes
arxiv-2102-11115.description: Abstract Semantic embeddings have advanced the state of the art for countless natural language processing tasks, and various extensions to multimodal domains, such as visual-semantic embeddings, have been proposed. While the power of visual-semantic embeddings comes from the distillation and enrichment of information through machine learning, their inner workings are poorly understood and there is a shortage of analysis tools.

arxiv-2104-10558.title: Contingencies from Observations: Tractable Contingency Planning with Learned Behavior Models
arxiv-2104-10558.creator: Nicholas Rhinehart ∗ , Jeff He ∗ , Charles Packer, Matthew A. Wright Rowan McAllister, Joseph E. Gonzalez, Sergey Levine
arxiv-2104-10558.description: Abstract Humans have a remarkable ability to make decisions by accurately reasoning about future events, including the future behaviors and states of mind of other agents. Consider driving a car through a busy intersection: it is necessary to reason about the physics of the vehicle, the intentions of other drivers, and their beliefs about your own intentions.

arxiv-2112-11398.title: Masanori Hanada,
arxiv-2112-11398.creator: a
arxiv-2112-11398.description: Abstract DMUS-MP-21/11 Global Symmetries and Partial Confinement Abstract In gauge theories, spontaneous breaking of the centre symmetry provides a precise definition of deconfinement. In large- N gauge theories, evidence has emerged recently that between confined and deconfined phases a partially-deconfined phase can appear, in which only a subset of colours deconfine.

arxiv-2310-00239.title: AdaptNet: Policy Adaptation for Physics-Based Character Control 543 Journal: TOG Volume: 42 6 112.1522 12 DOI: 10.1145/3618375 CCS: Computing methodologies Animation CCS: Computing methodologies Physical simulation CCS: Computing methodologies Reinforcement learning
arxiv-2310-00239.creator: Pei Xu, Kaixiang Xie, Sheldon Andrews, Paul G. Kry, Michael Neff, Morgan McGuire, Ioannis Karamouzas, Victor Zordan
arxiv-2310-00239.description: Abstract . Motivated by humans’ ability to adapt skills in the learning of new ones, this paper presents AdaptNet, an approach for modifying the latent space of existing policies to allow new behaviors to be quickly learned from like tasks in comparison to learning from scratch.

arxiv-2401-10903.title: Application of Machine Learning in Stock Market Forecasting: A Case Study of Disney Stock
arxiv-2401-10903.creator: Dengxin Huang
arxiv-2401-10903.description: Abstract ABSTRACT This document presents a stock market analysis conducted on a dataset consisting of 750 instances and 16 attributes donated in 2014-10-23. The analysis includes an exploratory data analysis (EDA) section, feature engineering, data preparation, model selection, and insights from the analysis. The Fama French 3-factor model is also utilized in the analysis.

arxiv-2402-01115.title: Interpretation of Intracardiac Electrograms Through Textual Representations
arxiv-2402-01115.creator: William Jongwon Han, Diana Gomez, Avi Alok, Chaojing Duan, Michael A. Rosenberg, Douglas Weber, Emerson Liu, Ding Zhao
arxiv-2402-01115.description: Abstract Understanding the irregular electrical activity of atrial fibrillation (AFib) has been a key challenge in electrocardiography. For serious cases of AFib, catheter ablations are performed to collect intracardiac electrograms (EGMs). EGMs offer intricately detailed and localized electrical activity of the heart and are an ideal modality for interpretable cardiac studies.

arxiv-2411-05429.title: Elementary proofs of the diameter bounds for the power graphs
arxiv-2411-05429.creator: Marco Barbieri, Kamilla Rekvényi
arxiv-2411-05429.description: Abstract . We give a simplified version of the proofs that, outside of their isolated vertices, the complement of the enhanced power graph and of the power graph are connected of diameter at most 3 3 . 2020 Mathematics Subject Classification 20D60, 05C25 1.

arxiv-2501-17604.title: nabqr: Python package for improving probabilistic forecasts Journal: SoftwareX
arxiv-2501-17604.creator: Bastian Schmidt Jørgensen, Jan Kloppenborg Møller, Peter Nystrup, Henrik Madsen
arxiv-2501-17604.description: Abstract We introduce the open-source Python package NABQR: Neural Adaptive Basis for (time-adaptive) Quantile Regression that provides reliable probabilistic forecasts. NABQR corrects ensembles (scenarios) with LSTM networks and then applies time-adaptive quantile regression to the corrected ensembles to obtain improved and more reliable forecasts.

arxiv-2504-13490.title: Early Timestep Zero-Shot Candidate Selection for Instruction-Guided Image Editing
arxiv-2504-13490.creator: Joowon Kim, Ziseok Lee, Donghyeon Cho, Sanghyun Jo, Yeonsung Jung Kyungsu Kim Eunho Yang
arxiv-2504-13490.description: Abstract Despite recent advances in diffusion models, achieving reliable image generation and editing results remains challenging due to the inherent diversity induced by stochastic noise in the sampling process. Particularly, instruction-guided image editing with diffusion models offers user-friendly editing capabilities, yet editing failures, such as background distortion, frequently occur across different attempts.

arxiv-2511-21408.title: Subjective Depth & Timescale Transformers: Learning Where and When to Compute
arxiv-2511-21408.creator: Frederico Wieser, Martin Benfeghoul, Haitham Bou Ammar, Jun Wang, Zafeirios Fountas, [2mm] AI Centre, Department of Computer Science, University College London, London, UK
arxiv-2511-21408.description: Abstract The rigid, uniform allocation of computation in standard Transformer (TF) architectures can limit their efficiency and scalability, particularly for large-scale models and long sequences. Addressing this, we introduce Subjective Depth Transformers (SDT) and Subjective Timescale Transformers (STT), two distinct architectures that leverage Bayesian surprise signals to dynamically route computation, learning where and when to compute within decoder-only TFs.

pmc-10638915.title: Elucidating the role of nicotinamide N-methyltransferase-p53 axis in the progression of chronic kidney disease
pmc-10638915.creator: Xin Zhen, Yuxiang Sun, Hongchun Lin, Yuebo Huang, Tianwei Liu, Yuanqing Li, Hui Peng
pmc-10638915.description: BackgroundChronic kidney disease (CKD) is a significant global health issue characterized by progressive loss of kidney function. Renal interstitial fibrosis (TIF) is a common feature of CKD, but current treatments are seldom effective in reversing TIF. Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT) has been found to increase in kidneys with TIF, but its role in renal fibrosis is unclear.

pmc-11513509.description: la pneumoniae strains in two patients from our Transplant Unit. Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) performed with Illumina MiSeq revealed that strains from each patient were the same and belonged to ST11. Our findings emphasize the value of supporting effective antibiotic stewardship programs based on surveillance cultures for detecting colonised patients.

pmc-11556111.title: Complete genome sequence of Thiomicrospira sp. strain V2501 isolated from 250 m below the ground level in Horonobe, Hokkaido, Japan
pmc-11556111.creator: Akio Ueno, Kiyoshi Sato, Shuji Tamamura, Takuma Murakami, Hidenori Inomata, Satoshi Tamazawa, Yuki Amano, Kazuya Miyakawa, Takeshi Naganuma, Toshifumi Igarashi
pmc-11556111.description: A thiosulfate-oxidizing bacterium, Thiomicrospira sp. strain V2501, was isolated from groundwater collected in a terrestrial deep subsurface environment. This strain was capable of chemolithoautotrophic growth on CO2 and thiosulfate. Here, we report the 2,240,851 bp complete genome sequence of strain V2501. ANNOUNCEMENT The genus Thiomicrospira (Tms.) (Gammaproteobacteria, Thiotrichales, and Piscirickettsiaceae) was originally described by Kuenen and Veldkamp (1).

pmc-11590328.title: Influence of the ligation sequence of the inferior mesenteric artery and vein on circulating tumor cells in laparoscopic rectal cancer surgery: a prospective pilot study
pmc-11590328.creator: Tao Pan, Chang-bo Nie, Chao Liu, Hai Hu
pmc-11590328.description: BackgroundThere is no regulation in the current guidelines on the sequence of ligation of the inferior mesenteric artery and vein during rectal cancer surgery owing to a lack of sufficient evidence. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) in peripheral blood can be used as potential indicators for predicting prognosis in colorectal cancer patients.

pmc-11600580.title: Dual-modal overcoming of physical barriers for improved photodynamic cancer therapy via soft organosilica nanocapsules
pmc-11600580.creator: Wei Lu, Yang Li, Xiaojun Zhang, Ning Wang, Dong Chen, Yatong Zhao, Guang Li, Xuzhi Shi, Xiaobo Ma, Xiaodan Su, Feng Wang, Chuqiang Shu, Kun Chen
pmc-11600580.description: Amidst the burgeoning field of cancer nanomedicine, dense extracellular matrices and anomalous vascular structures in the tumor microenvironment (TME) present substantial physical barriers to effective therapeutic delivery. These physical barriers hinder the optimal bioavailability of nanomedicine. Here, we propose a pioneering dual-modal strategy for overcoming physical barriers via soft organosilica nanocapsules (SMONs).

pmc-11603116.creator: Kasja Malkoc, Michaela Hau, Scott McWilliams, Edyta Teresa Sadowska, Maciej Dzialo, Barbara Pierce, Lisa Trost, Ulf Bauchinger, Eve Udino, Stefania Casagrande
pmc-11603116.description: reat tits (Parus major). They captured great tits in winter to measure their night-time RMR with traditional respirometry, at thermoneutrality (20°C) for the first 4 h, and at 8°C for the remaining 4 h of measurements. Immediately after RMR measurements birds were blood-sampled and mitochondrial respiration states assessed in red blood cells at 41°C with high-resolution respirometry.

pmc-11716643.creator: Dylan X Guan, Matthew E Peters, G Bruce Pike, Eric E Smith, Zahinoor Ismail

pmc-12630658.description: Abstract rules are central to human language, allowing for the generalization of grammatical rules to novel contexts. However, the evolutionary origin of the ability to learn and generalize these rules is unclear, and evidence for these capacities in nonhuman primates is equivocal.

pmc-12677840.title: Design and Evaluation of Sticky End‐Type Bivalent DNA Aptamers Containing M08s‐1 as Anticoagulant Agents
pmc-12677840.creator: Maasa Yokomori, Mizuki Murasawa, Muneyuki Matsuo, Masanobu Nagano, Keitaro Yoshimoto
pmc-12677840.description: Aptamer is a promising therapeutic modality, offering strong target affinity and target versatility. In the previous studies, DNA aptamers with potent thrombin inhibitory activity, M08s‐1 and its bivalent derivatives, have been developed as novel anticoagulant agents. Among them, the heterobivalent aptamer Pse08‐29 exhibits the most potent ex vivo anticoagulant activity, surpassing the approved drug argatroban.

pmc-12751605.title: Exploring doctors experiences of transitioning to full time research and back to clinical practice: a qualitative study
pmc-12751605.creator: Maria Farren, Cathal Darby, Shahad Al Tikriti, Mary Higgins
pmc-12751605.description: BackgroundDespite the growing interest in research degrees among clinicians, little is knowns about doctors’ lived experiences transitioning between clinical practice and full-time research. Understanding these transitions is essential for developing appropriate support structure and optimising career pathways. This study aimed to explore the experience for doctors of transitioning to research and back to clinical work.

pmc-13074262.title: In Situ Performic Acid Epoxidation of Polyfarnesene: Evidence of Oxirane Ring Instability and Its Impact on Multifunctional Polymer Composition
pmc-13074262.creator: Geilza A. Porto, Luiz Guilherme A. de Paula, Luciano N. Batista, Marcos L. Dias
pmc-13074262.description: Polyfarnesene, a bio-based polymer, was epoxidized in situ using performic acid to investigate oxirane ring formation, stability, and the role of its bottlebrush architecture in the kinetics. The reaction reached a maximum epoxidation degree of ~20% after 6 h but underwent side reactions, producing hydroxyl and formic ester groups.

pmc-13384105.description: Gallium oxide (Ga2O3) is an ultrawide-bandgap semiconductor with strong potential for electronic and optoelectronic applications. The metastable corundum α-phase is particularly attractive for alloying and bandgap engineering but suffers from limited thermal stability. In this work, the phase stability of α-(FexGa1−x)2O3 thin films grown by mist chemical vapor deposition is systematically studied using experiments and density functional theory.
